newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends shade higher in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends shade higher in light trade.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended a shade higher on Monday at 26.363 from 26.364 due to the lack of incentive to buy up the dollar after the Central Bank's strong intervention last Wednesday, traders said.
"After the Central Bank was firm at 26.37 last Wednesday, the market didn't have the appetite to buy up the dollar," a dealer said.
The Central Bank sold heavily last Wednesday after the peso slumped to 26.37 as arbitrage money left. The peso was pounded due to its smaller interest premium versus the U.S. dollar.
Banks were closed Thursday and Friday thereafter for the Easter holidays.
The peso, however, slipped to 26.367 in intra-day trades as it was pulled down by a $20.7-million sale to oil firms.
Market volume thinned to $93.50 million from $305.40 million due to holidays in Hong Kong and London.
On Tuesday, the peso will take its cue from any moves of the Central Bank to adjust its overnight rates, dealers said.
